lines.text: Your slice isn't always your grip.
The ball starts left or straight, then curves hard right.
So you aim further left to allow for it.
Watch the start of your downswing.
Your shoulders throw the club out toward the ball.
The club comes down above the line it went up on.
So it cuts across the ball, out to in.
Leave the face open to that path and it slices.
Ben Hogan's book pictured this in 1957.
Resting on your shoulders, down to the ball.
The idea: swing under it, and never break it.
Staying under it takes practice, the app I'm building shows you the plane before each slice drill, so try this.
From the top, let your trail elbow drop toward your hip.
Feel the club arrive from inside the ball.
Many slices start at the top.
